earlier_scan.source_named: Only survey wordlists (Lee 2006 SIL survei bahasa Emem; Smits & Voorhoeve 1994; Galis 1956; Voorhoeve 1975); no phonological description covering stress located.

sources.citation: Lebold, Randy & Myung Young Lee. 2016. Survey Report on the Emem Language of Papua, Indonesia. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2016-008. Dallas: SIL International. 47 pp. (published English version of Lee 2006 'Laporan survei pada bahasa Emem')
sources.note: Nothing. A sociolinguistic (Phase I rapid-appraisal) survey: no phonology, no mention of stress/accent/tone anywhere in the prose (grep zero hits). Appendix B (txt lines 1332-1616) gives four IPA village wordlists (Yuruf, Umuaf, Yambraf Dua, Semografi) that carry primary-stress marks; my own tally of 320 polysyllabic tokens with one mark: 135 initial, 134 final, 51 medial, i.e. no fixed position visible, but the authors make no claim about it.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2007. Change Request 2007-215: adopted update [enr], rename Emumu -> Emem (2008-01-14). SIL International.
sources.note: Nothing; name change only, citing the draft SIL survey report as its sole source (txt line 156).

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Languages of Irian Jaya, Checklist: preliminary classification, language maps, wordlists. Pacific Linguistics B-31. Canberra: ANU. Chapters 05 (Non-Austronesian checklist) and 06 of the papuaweb split, image scans scanned at 200 dpi.
sources.note: Nothing. Entry '111. EMUMU (Kiamerop), IX b + 1100' on p. 44 (scanned page p05-24, under 'AS. PAUWASI STOCK / AS.2. Eastern Family') gives 'Dialects: ?' and a list of 20 villages; no phonology, no wordlist for Emumu in these chapters. scanned grep for stress/accent: zero hits.
Nothing; 0 descriptive references. Alternative names Emem, Imimkal, Kiamerop; classification commentary from Voorhoeve 1971; endangerment from Voorhoeve 1975 via Campbell et al. 2022.
Nothing on phonology; distribution (5 villages in Web District, Keerom), North/South Emem dialects, ~2,000 speakers (2005); references only Lee 2006 and Lebold & Lee 2016.

Nothing on stress; notes the Indonesian Pauwasi languages are 'poorly attested' and that the best-described Pauwasi language is Karkar(-Yuri) in PNG; references Wurm 1975, Ross 2005, Wichmann 2013, Foley 2018, Pawley & Hammarström 2018.
